observations.content: User supplied context-only reference packets (preparation turns 1–8 of 12) for a later implementation task; no implementation request was made in this chunk.

Later implementation requirement: observer and consolidator workers must run with the owning session’s resolved `.memory/<sessionId>/` root as cwd, ensuring worker-session discovery, transient result/cost IPC, and consolidator filesystem access are session-scoped; use the runtime-resolved root, create it before spawning even when fresh and empty, and preserve worker model, prompt, environment, result handoff, cancellation, and exit handling.

Observational-memory project uses a default-OFF per-session `/om` gate persisted as `om.enabled`; observer subprocesses distill fixed token-bounded conversation chunks into branch-local ledger observations, while deterministic compaction injects journey, memory map, and active observations; a background consolidator promotes oldest overflow to `.memory/<sessionId>/` topic files and tombstones the handed active batch.

Long-term memory is isolated by immutable session-header id under `.memory/<sessionId>/`; forked sessions seed the parent memory root once, excluding transient `.runs/`, and existing roots are never reseeded. Runtime stores the resolved root and passes it to workers through `OM_MEMORY_DIR`.

Worker runs are ordinary recorded headless pi sessions launched with bespoke `child_process.spawn`; the observer receives the chunk in its recorded `-p` user prompt, while consolidator edits are constrained to the session memory root. Worker cost is handed back through `.runs` IPC and recorded in `om.cost` entries across the whole session.
